text:
Zach Benson has 15 points in 16 games and only two goals, which tells you most of what you need to know about his season so far. The 21-year-old from Chilliwack is playing 20:07 a night (up from 15:53), he has a six-game point streak, and the Sabres are winning their minutes when he plays: 59.7 percent of the five-on-five expected goals, 14 points better than without him. On November 6 he set up Josh Norris alone in front for a goal that The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn called a great play.

Two things are out of line, in opposite directions. His own finishing is cold, two goals on 6.46 expected, shooting 5.1 percent, and goals tend to follow chances. His teammates' finishing is hot: Buffalo has scored 10.8 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that will fade. Net, the points should hold up even as the mix changes.

Evolving-Hockey rated his play-driving in the 98th percentile among forwards last season, so the underlying game is not new. He missed a practice early this month and was cleared to play November 4. Watch the goal column; it is due.
headline: Benson is making everyone around him score
